original_source_contract.future_candidate_condition: The actual CONFIG must pin its published HEAD/tree/format-base and exact parent roster. The script reparses the actual checked-out workflow and refuses disagreement; this audit transfers no test result from 5daade.

confirmed_corrections.finding: Python check_output(... rustc -Vv, timeout=60) implicitly kills a timed-out child although no explicit killpg remains.
confirmed_corrections.final: Operator rustc version lookup now uses recorded() and the unmodified source-bound hepta_ci_exec.py, as does the Root lookup. The outer harness has no Rust signal/kill path.

confirmed_corrections.finding: A timed-out/truncated ordinary test could previously fall through to Root Cargo after recording failure.
confirmed_corrections.final: Any original recorder timeout/truncation/running/interruption or missing terminal record sets completion_unknown; later recorded Cargo dispatches refuse. A normal terminal test failure may still collect distinct Root results, but the aggregate result stays failed.

confirmed_corrections.finding: An uncertain Root execution must not be collected or have its records/fixtures mutated while it can still be active.
confirmed_corrections.final: Unknown completion skips the JUnit collector and all chown/unmount/remove actions. The retained original Popen is only observed; no retry, signal, subsequent Cargo or later cleanup is authorized by its eventual exit.

reviewed_guards: Fresh task directory and exact key/value CONFIG; separate operator and Root targets; original pinned Rust 1.96.0 checked in both UID contexts.
Exact published commit object/tree, clean checkout, no skip-worktree/assume-unchanged/unmerged entries, and every tracked file's physical Git-blob bytes and mode are checked before and after.
Actual source tools/checkers and external executable bytes are pinned before/after; maintenance dirty output stops behavioral dispatch and preserves the raw patch/postimages.
Six-crate maintenance and binary check, all four existing QA suites, and the original unchanged full caller verifier precede same-source helper construction and behavior tests.
Ordinary suite uses original just test --locked --offline, all six packages, --lib, retries 0, full original no-fail-fast wrapper. It retains normal ignored-test scope.
Root commands enter actual sudo UID0, emit fsynced UID/eUID proof, use a distinct Root-owned target, and compare the actual Root toolchain output to the operator's pinned version.

Fresh original Cargo metadata plus nextest list compile the two selected Root library binaries. Exact package IDs/library kinds and target-contained binary bytes are pinned; actual ignored filter matches must equal all 17 frozen parent names.

The original just/nextest wrapper itself already uses fresh --cargo-metadata with graph-free package filters; this does not use --binaries-metadata/archive build replay. RustTestSuiteSummary flattens its binary fields in the machine-readable JSON.

Both suites move aside old JUnit before launch. The unmodified collector requires exact source-head identity, original just/test/--locked command, report mtime inside the actual execution interval, matching terminal pass/fail counts, and at least one executed test.
Root JUnit's executed names must exactly equal the 17 original parents, independently of the prior list; helpers are not added as parent passes. Actual Root binaries are rehashed after just test.

Root fixture cleanup is limited to the inode-proven directory freshly created by this attempt. Both bind unmounts run independently, removal requires successful unmount checks, and chown is limited to this attempt's records and source nextest reports.

Original recorder root completion must be terminal and neither timed out nor output-truncated before mutable cleanup is permitted. Unknown completion remains unknown even if read-only final source observations are possible.

limits.explanation: The intentional wait for an already-running original launcher can outlive the dispatch budget. Such an attempt is incomplete/failed and cannot be relabeled PASS or guaranteed process termination. The source executor itself states that escaped sessions require an external sandbox.
